_readme: DRAFT, NOT VERIFIED. Built from web research (see 'sources' per entry), not a domain expert.
Do NOT use this to fetch/label training data without review by someone who reads Sinhala
and/or has Sri Lankan herpetological field knowledge -- a wrong entry here would silently
pollute the training set with images of the wrong species.
confidence: 'high' = direct name match against a cited source. 'moderate' = same genus/name
family confirmed but exact species among close relatives not pinned down. 'unresolved' = no
confident source found; scientific_name is null, do not guess.
IMPORTANT FINDING: at least one source (a Sri Lankan cat-snake reference, see naga-mapila/
le-mapila entries) states local names like 'mapila' are used inconsistently -- the same
species can go by several different local names, and the same local name is sometimes used
for different species/genera depending on region. This means our 43 class labels may not be
a clean 1:1 mapping to 43 biological species -- flagged for review, see conversation notes.

cobra.notes: Unambiguous, English name used directly as the class.

thith-polanga.notes: Russell's viper, one of the 5 medically important species.

thel-karawala.notes: Common krait, one of the 5 medically important species.

kunakatuwa.notes: Hump-nosed viper, one of the 5 medically important species.

wali-polanga.notes: Likely 'veli polonga' (saw-scaled viper, one of the 5 medically important species) -- spelling variant, not a direct match, double-check.

diyabariya.notes: Revised from initial guess 'Xenochrophis piscator'/'Fowlea piscator' (checkered keelback): that species has only 1 iNaturalist record ever in Sri Lanka despite being common region-wide, while Fowlea asperrima (Sri Lanka-endemic keelback) has 134 research-grade Sri Lanka observations -- almost certainly the actual local match for 'diyabariya', but still worth a human sanity-check.

lanka-diyabariya.notes: Likely another keelback/water-snake species (Xenochrophis/Fowlea spp.) given 'diyabariya' root, but not confirmed which one.

tikiri-diyabariya.notes: Same family as above, 'tikiri' may mean small/juvenile -- could even be a size descriptor rather than a distinct species. Needs verification.

naga-mapila.notes: SEE _readme WARNING: one source lists Boiga forsteni's Sinhala names as 'Naga Mapila' AND 'Le Mapila' both -- overlaps with our separate le-mapila class. Needs disambiguation, not just acceptance.

le-mapila.notes: SEE _readme WARNING -- same overlap concern as naga-mapila. These may not be biologically distinct; needs expert review before use.

kana-ulla.notes: Genus-level only: blind snakes (Indotyphlops/Grypotyphlops spp.), exact species not identified.

alu-randanakaya.notes: Likely another Lycodon (wolf snake) species/color variant given the '-randanakaya' root, exact species not identified.

mal-sara.notes: Described as 'ornate flying snake' by a source but scientific name not stated directly there -- Chrysopelea ornata is the standard match for that English name, worth confirming.

thuru-haldanda.notes: Likely an Ahaetulla (vine/whip snake) species given the '-haldanda' root (possibly meaning whip/cane), not confirmed.

panduru-haldanda.notes: Same family concern as above, different species/variant.

kandukara-mukalan-thelissa.notes: 'mukalan thelissa' matched a source's name for Hypnale zara; 'kandukara' prefix not explained by that source.

depath-naya.notes: No source found. Contains 'naya' (cobra root) but likely a different, unrelated species given compound name patterns elsewhere -- do not assume Naja naja.

kaha-mapila.notes: No source found. 'mapila' root suggests a cat snake (Boiga) species, but per the naga-mapila/le-mapila warning, do not assume without verification.

palabariya.notes: No source found. Root differs from 'diyabariya' (confirmed keelback) -- do not assume the same family.

rana-mapila.notes: No source found. One source mentioned 'Ran Mapila'/'Garandi Mapila' as Sinhala names for Boiga trigonata (gamma cat snake) -- close but not an exact spelling match to 'rana-mapila', needs verification not assumption.

kunu-diya-kaluwa.notes: No source found. 'diya' root suggests a water-associated species, unconfirmed.
